newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sorghum continues to fall - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sorghum continues to fall - Grainco.

text.p: International market pressure continued to cause domestic Australian sorghum values to drift lower, Queensland grain cooperative Grainco said in its weekly market report.

Added to pressure on the U.S. corn futures market, domestic consumer interest in new crop sorghum remained quiet as most buyers waited to see what the winter harvest of feed barley and feed wheat brought, Grainco trading manager Rob Brealey said.
The medium-term direction appeared steadily lower, he said.
Reports of several sales of new crop barley from Australia at levels lower than market expectations added a bearish tone to an already pressured domestic market, he said.

With harvest to start in some areas this week or in the next 10 days, most consumers were still standing aside in anticipation of harvest pressure on domestic values. There was little to suggest a rebound from current levels in the short-term, he said.
Problems in Canada with the barley and wheat harvest was also not benefiting feed barley values at present, he said, although they gave some support to malting barley values.
In cottonseed, export market price sentiment remains softer than in the domestic market, with stocks concentrated in several larger trader hands.
Chickpea prices remain under pressure as the first receipts of new crop are delivered.
Domestic Australian oilseed values had come back on further erosion in the futures market.
